docs.title: vexy-pdfsvgpy
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy is a Python library and command-line tool that converts files between PDF, SVG, PNG and JPG. You call one function, convert(), or one command, vexy-pdfsvgpy convert. The extension of the output file decides the target format.

Every backend installs as a normal pip wheel. The package does not need Cairo, Poppler, Ghostscript or any other system library.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Input Output Default backend PDF PNG pymupdf PDF SVG pymupdf SVG PNG resvg-py SVG PDF pymupdf PNG or JPG SVG (traced) vtracer PNG or JPG PDF (wrapped) pymupdf PDF PDF (normalized) pymupdf SVG SVG (normalized) pymupdf

The CLI also splits a multi-page PDF into one file per page and merges several PDFs into one.

docs.title: One call
docs.text:
from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert

convert(input="report.pdf", output="report.png")   # rasterize page 1
convert(input="logo.svg", output="logo.pdf")        # SVG to PDF
convert(input="report.pdf", output="report.svg")    # PDF page 1 to SVG

docs.title: From the shell
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report.png
vexy-pdfsvgpy split --input report.pdf --out_dir ./pages/
vexy-pdfsvgpy merge --inputs "a.pdf,b.pdf" --output book.pdf

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
Many PDF and SVG toolchains fail once they leave the machine they were built on: libcairo is missing, the Poppler version differs, or a Homebrew formula has changed. vexy-pdfsvgpy follows one rule: after pip install, it works. Each backend was chosen because it ships as a self-contained wheel.

The cost is fidelity in some directions. PDF to SVG is lossy: groups are flattened, and with text_as="paths" the text becomes outlines that can no longer be selected. See Backends.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
Everything on this page is importable from vexy_pdfsvgpy unless a module path is given.

from vexy_pdfsvgpy import (
    convert, plan, execute, Step,
    FormatSpec, Packaging, Content, Hint, Hints,
    Capability, Document, Page,
    VexyError, InvalidInput, UnsupportedConversion, BackendFailure, UnsupportedOnPlatform,
    __version__,
)

docs.title: convert()
docs.text:
convert(
    input: str | Path | None = None,
    output: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    vinput: str | None = None,
    voutput: str | None = None,
    binput: str | None = None,
    boutput: str | None = None,
    hints: str | Hints | None = None,
    **options,
) -> Path | list[Path]

The single entry point. It takes an input path and an output path, works out the formats, plans the conversion and runs it.

Parameter Meaning input Source file or directory. Must exist. output Destination file, or a directory for packaging d. vinput, binput Input format spec. vinput wins if both are set. Required when input is a directory. voutput, boutput Output format spec. voutput wins if both are set. hints Backend preference, as a string such as "re,mu" or a Hints object. See Backends. recursive Option. With a directory input, search subdirectories. glob Option. With a directory input, select files with this glob pattern. **options Everything else is passed to the backend function. See below.

Return value:

  • One input file: the output Path.
  • Several input files (directory input): a list of output paths.

What convert() does, in order:

  1. Checks that input and output are given and that input exists. Otherwise it raises InvalidInput.
  2. Builds the input spec from vinput, binput, or the input extension.
  3. Builds the output spec from voutput, boutput, or the output extension.
  4. Collects the input files. A directory is expanded only for input packaging d.
  5. Calls plan() and execute() for each file.

docs.title: Backend keyword arguments
docs.text:
Options other than recursive and glob go to the backend function unchanged. Use them to set the page, resolution or tracing parameters:

# Second page at 150 dpi with pymupdf
convert(input="report.pdf", output="page2.png", page=1, dpi=150)

# SVG at 1024 px wide with resvg
convert(input="logo.svg", output="logo.png", width=1024)

# PDF page to SVG with outlined text
convert(input="report.pdf", output="report.svg", text_as="paths")

The accepted names depend on which backend runs; see Backend details. If the backend does not accept a keyword, the call raises BackendFailure with the TypeError message. For example, dpi works with pymupdf for SVG to PNG but not with resvg, which takes width.

Same-format conversions (PDF to PDF, SVG to SVG) ignore options.

docs.title: FormatSpec
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class FormatSpec:
    format: Literal["pdf", "svg", "png", "jpg"]
    packaging: Packaging = Packaging.D
    content: Content | None = None
Member Description FormatSpec.parse(s) Parse a string such as "pdf_mo". Raises InvalidInput. FormatSpec.from_extension(path) Default spec for .pdf, .svg, .png, .jpg, .jpeg. str(spec) Shortest canonical form; round-trips with parse(). spec.is_vector True for pdf and svg. spec.is_bitmap True for png and jpg. 
spec = FormatSpec.parse("svg_lt")
spec.format       # 'svg'
spec.packaging    # <Packaging.L: 'l'>
spec.content      # <Content.T: 't'>
str(spec)         # 'svg_lt'

Packaging has the members D, M, L, S. Content has O, T, B. Both are StrEnums whose values are the lowercase letters.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
Hints.parse("re,mu")            # Hints(preferences=(Hint.RE, Hint.MU))
Hints.parse(["ap", Hint.MU])    # strings and Hint members can be mixed
Hints.parse(None)               # empty Hints, which is falsy

Hint is a StrEnum with RE, MU, PK, AP, CA, GS. hints.pick(candidates) returns the first preference that appears in candidates, or None.

docs.title: plan() and execute()
docs.text:
Use these to inspect or reuse a conversion without running it immediately.

from pathlib import Path
from vexy_pdfsvgpy import FormatSpec, Hints, plan, execute

steps = plan(FormatSpec.parse("svg"), FormatSpec.parse("png"), Hints.parse("mu"), options={"dpi": 96})
for step in steps:
    print(step.capability, step.backend.name, step.kwargs)
# svg_to_png pymupdf {'dpi': 96}

execute(steps, Path("logo.svg"), Path("logo.png"))
  • plan(input_spec, output_spec, hints=None, *, options=None) -> list[Step] returns one Step. When both formats are the same it uses the normalize capability, without options. It raises UnsupportedConversion when no direct path exists, for example PNG to PNG or PDF to JPG.
  • execute(steps, src, dst) -> Path runs the steps and returns dst. Exceptions from a backend that are not already BackendFailure are wrapped in BackendFailure.
  • Step is a frozen dataclass with capability, backend and kwargs. backend has name, hint and func.
  • Capability is the StrEnum of capability names listed in Backends.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors derive from VexyError.

Class Raised when InvalidInput A path is missing, a format spec or hint is invalid, an extension is unknown, or a directory has no matching files. UnsupportedConversion No backend is registered for the conversion. BackendFailure A backend raised. Attributes: backend (name), op (capability), original (the exception). The message reads [backend] op failed: original. UnsupportedOnPlatform Defined for platform-specific operations. The Apple backend currently reports non-macOS use through BackendFailure instead. 
from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert, VexyError

try:
    convert(input="scan.png", output="scan.png")
except VexyError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e)
# UnsupportedConversion identity conversion png → png is not supported

docs.title: Document and Page
docs.text:
Document and Page are passive containers for in-memory pages. convert() does not use them yet.

  • Page(content, kind, width, height, dpi=None, label=None). content is bytes for PDF and bitmaps and str for SVG. width and height are points for vector pages and pixels for bitmaps.
  • Document(pages=[], source=None, spec=None) supports len(), bool(), page_count, kind, add(page), Document.empty(spec=None) and Document.from_path(path, *, spec=None). from_path does not read the file; it inserts one placeholder page so that kind is known.

docs.title: Reshape operations
docs.text:
vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.reshape combines and splits documents directly, outside convert():

Function Result pages2docs_pdf(src, out_dir, *, stem=None) One PDF per page, via pikepdf. Returns the list of paths. docs2pages_pdf(srcs, dst) One multi-page PDF, via pikepdf. docs2layers_pdf(srcs, dst, *, labels=None) One page with each source's first page in its own optional content group (OCG). Default labels: Layer 1, Layer 2, and so on. docs2layers_svg(srcs, dst, *, labels=None) One SVG with each source in an Inkscape layer: <g inkscape:groupmode="layer" inkscape:label="...">. Size and viewBox come from the first source. layers2docs_svg(src, out_dir) One SVG per Inkscape layer, named {stem}-{label}.svg. Falls back to top-level <g> elements when there are no Inkscape layers. 
from pathlib import Path
from vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations import reshape

reshape.docs2layers_pdf(
    [Path("base.pdf"), Path("overlay.pdf")],
    Path("layered.pdf"),
    labels=["Base", "Overlay"],
)

docs.title: Other modules
docs.text:
• vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.regularize: regularize_pdf(src, dst, *, backend="pymupdf") with "pymupdf" or "apple", and regularize_svg(src, dst, *, backend="pymupdf", width=2048) with "pymupdf" or "resvg". The resvg variant renders the SVG to PNG and wraps it as a base64 <image> in a new SVG.
  • vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.color: ColorOptions, parse_color() and apply_color_bitmap(). Not called by convert() yet.
  • vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.sizecrop: SizeCropOptions, parse_dim(), resolve_dim(), compute_scale(), resolve_margins(), apply_sizecrop_pdf(). Not called by convert() yet.
  • vexy_pdfsvgpy.paths: render_output(template, *, stem, page, ...) fills {stem}, {page}, {index}, {backend}, {ext} and {scale} placeholders in an output path. It is not called by convert() yet.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy is a thin layer over a fixed set of backends. A call passes through four stages: parse the formats, plan, dispatch, execute.

convert(input, output, ...)
   │
   ├─ FormatSpec.parse / from_extension   →  input_spec, output_spec
   ├─ Hints.parse                          →  hints
   ├─ _gather_inputs                       →  [file, ...]
   │
   └─ for each file:
        plan(input_spec, output_spec, hints, options)
           └─ dispatch.resolve(capability, hints)  →  BackendFn
        execute(steps, src, dst)
           └─ backend.func(src, dst, **kwargs)

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text: Module Role vexy_pdfsvgpy/__init__.py convert(), input gathering, public exports types.py FormatSpec, Packaging, Content, Hint, Hints pipeline.py plan(), execute(), Step dispatch.py Capability, the backend table, resolve() backends/ One module per library: pymupdf_backend, pdfium_backend, resvg_backend, pypdf_backend, pikepdf_backend, vtracer_backend, wrap_backend, apple_backend, cairo_backend, ghostscript_backend operations/ reshape, regularize, sizecrop, color document.py Document, Page paths.py Output file name templating errors.py VexyError and subclasses cli.py The Fire CLI class and main()

docs.title: Follow one call
docs.text:
Take convert(input="logo.svg", output="logo.png", hints="mu", dpi=96).

  1. Parse. No vinput or binput is given, so FormatSpec.from_extension("logo.svg") returns svg (packaging d, content o). The output becomes png (packaging d). Hints.parse("mu") returns (Hint.MU,).
  2. Gather. The input is a file, so the list is [Path("logo.svg")].
  3. Plan. The formats differ, so plan() looks up ("svg", "png") in its table of direct conversions and finds Capability.SVG_TO_PNG.
  4. Dispatch. resolve() reads the backends for svg_to_png: resvg (re), pymupdf (mu), cairo (ca). The first hint, mu, matches pymupdf, so the step uses pymupdf_backend.svg_to_png.
  5. Execute. execute() calls svg_to_png(Path("logo.svg"), Path("logo.png"), dpi=96). The backend renders the SVG with PyMuPDF and saves the PNG.
  6. Return. convert() returns Path("logo.png").

Without hints="mu", step 4 picks resvg, and dpi=96 fails in step 5 because resvg_backend.svg_to_png takes width, not dpi.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
plan() knows two kinds of conversion:

  • Same format (pdf→pdf, svg→svg): the normalize capability for that format. Options are not forwarded. PNG→PNG and JPG→JPG raise UnsupportedConversion.
  • Direct conversion, one step:
From To Capability pdf png pdf_to_png pdf svg pdf_to_svg svg pdf svg_to_pdf svg png svg_to_png png, jpg svg png_to_svg_trace png, jpg pdf bitmap_to_pdf

Any other pair raises UnsupportedConversion, for example pdf→jpg or svg→jpg. JPG is accepted as an input but no conversion writes JPG yet.

execute() accepts several steps and writes intermediate files next to the destination as <dst>.step<i>.tmp. plan() currently returns one step only.

docs.title: Dispatch
docs.text:
dispatch._load_table() imports each backend module inside try/except ImportError and registers its functions. A missing optional library therefore does not break import vexy_pdfsvgpy. The table is built on first use and cached.

resolve(cap, hints):

  1. Gets the backend list for the capability. If it is empty, raises UnsupportedConversion.
  2. For each hint in order, returns the first backend with that hint.
  3. Otherwise returns the first backend in the list.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Backends raise RuntimeError with a [backend] prefix. execute() wraps anything that is not already a BackendFailure as BackendFailure(backend.name, capability, original). The CLI catches VexyError, prints the class name and message, and returns exit code 1.

docs.title: Design rules
docs.text:
These rules come from SPEC.md and IDEA.md in the repository:

  • Every default backend installs as a wheel with no system library and no post-install step.
  • One backend per capability by default. Alternatives exist only where a real trade-off is worth exposing, and you choose them with a hint, not a configuration file.
  • Inputs are parsed into typed objects (FormatSpec, Hints) at the boundary.
  • Backend exceptions do not leak; they are wrapped in the narrow VexyError hierarchy.
  • No global configuration, plugin registry or caching layer beyond the dispatch table.

docs.title: Backends
docs.text: Each conversion is one capability, such as pdf_to_png. Each capability has an ordered list of backend functions. Without hints, the first backend in the list runs. A hint moves another backend to the front when a real speed or fidelity trade-off exists.

docs.title: Capability table
docs.text:
This is the table the dispatcher builds on import. The left-most backend is the default.

Capability Backends, in order (hint code) Default output pdf_to_png pymupdf (mu), pdfium (mu), apple (ap), ghostscript (gs) Page 1 at 300 dpi pdf_to_svg pymupdf (mu) Page 1, text kept as <text> svg_to_png resvg (re), pymupdf (mu), cairo (ca) 2048 px wide svg_to_pdf pymupdf (mu), cairo (ca) One-page PDF png_to_svg_trace vtracer (re) Color spline tracing; used for PNG and JPG input bitmap_to_pdf wrap (mu) Bitmap placed in a PDF page by pymupdf pdf_normalize pymupdf (mu), apple (ap), ghostscript (gs) clean=True, deflate=True, garbage=4 svg_normalize pymupdf (mu) First page re-emitted as SVG pdf_split pypdf (pk), pikepdf (pk), apple (ap) Not used by convert() pdf_merge pikepdf (pk), pypdf (pk), apple (ap) Not used by convert() png_to_svg_wrap wrap (mu) Not used by convert()

The split and merge CLI subcommands call pikepdf directly through vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.reshape, not through the dispatcher.

pdfium shares the mu hint with pymupdf, which comes first, so a hint cannot select pdfium. Call vexy_pdfsvgpy.backends.pdfium_backend.pdf_to_png() directly to use it.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
A hint is a two-letter code. You can pass several, separated by commas; the order sets the priority.

Code Backend mu PyMuPDF re resvg (and vtracer, which is registered under re) pk pypdf / pikepdf ap Apple PDFKit and Quartz (macOS only) ca CairoSVG (needs the cairo extra) gs Ghostscript (needs the ghostscript extra)

The dispatcher goes through your hints in order. For the first hint that matches a backend of the capability, that backend runs. If no hint matches, the default runs. An unknown code raises InvalidInput.

from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert

# SVG to PNG with pymupdf instead of resvg
convert(input="logo.svg", output="logo.png", hints="mu")

# Try Apple first, then pymupdf
convert(input="report.pdf", output="report.png", hints="ap,mu")

From the shell, use --hint:

vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input logo.svg --output logo.png --hint mu

docs.title: PyMuPDF (pymupdf)
docs.text:
The default for most capabilities.

  • pdf_to_png(src, dst, *, page=0, dpi=300, alpha=False)
  • pdf_to_svg(src, dst, *, page=0, text_as=None). With text_as="paths" the SVG contains outlines; any other value keeps <text> elements that reference the PDF fonts.
  • svg_to_png(src, dst, *, dpi=300, alpha=True)
  • svg_to_pdf(src, dst)
  • pdf_normalize(src, dst)
  • svg_normalize(src, dst, *, page=0, text_as=None)

docs.title: resvg (resvg-py)
docs.text:
The default SVG rasterizer.

  • svg_to_png(src, dst, *, width=2048) renders at the given pixel width.

Some SVGs set width and height in pt, which resvg rejects with an "invalid size" error. The backend then rewrites those attributes as plain numbers and renders again once.

docs.title: pypdfium2 (pdfium)
docs.text: • pdf_to_png(src, dst, *, page=0, dpi=300) renders with scale=dpi/72 and saves through Pillow.

docs.title: vtracer
docs.text:
• trace(src, dst, *, colormode="color", mode="spline", filter_speckle=4, color_precision=6, layer_difference=16, corner_threshold=60, length_threshold=4.0, max_iterations=10, splice_threshold=45, path_precision=8)

colormode is "color" or "binary". mode is "spline", "polygon" or "pixel". Pass any of these as keyword arguments to convert() when the input is PNG or JPG and the output is SVG:

convert(input="logo.png", output="logo.svg", colormode="binary", mode="polygon")

docs.title: wrap
docs.text:
Places a bitmap in a vector container without tracing.

  • png_to_pdf(src, dst) and jpg_to_pdf(src, dst) open the bitmap with pymupdf and save it as a PDF.
  • png_to_svg(src, dst), jpg_to_svg(src, dst) and bitmap_to_svg(src, dst, *, mime=None) embed the image as a base64 <image> in a minimal SVG with the bitmap's pixel size.

docs.title: pikepdf and pypdf
docs.text: Lossless page operations. split(src, out_dir, *, stem=None) writes {stem}-pikepdf-page-{NN}.pdf (or -pypdf- for pypdf). merge(srcs, dst) concatenates the pages of each input in order. pikepdf_backend.overlay_pages(base, overlays, dst) also exists.

docs.title: Apple (ap)
docs.text:
Uses PDFKit and CoreGraphics through PyObjC. It is installed only on macOS. On other platforms the module imports, but each call raises an error that convert() reports as BackendFailure.

  • pdf_to_png(src, dst, *, page=0, width=2048)
  • pdf_normalize(src, dst)
  • split(src, out_dir, *, stem=None) and merge(srcs, dst)

docs.title: Cairo (ca) and Ghostscript (gs)
docs.text:
Optional, behind the cairo and ghostscript extras. Both modules are always registered, but they import their library only when called. Without the extra, a ca or gs hint fails at conversion time.

  • Cairo: svg_to_png(src, dst, *, dpi=300), svg_to_pdf(src, dst)
  • Ghostscript: pdf_to_png(src, dst, *, page=0, dpi=300), pdf_normalize(src, dst, *, text_as=None)

docs.title: Lossy paths
docs.text: PDF to SVG is lossy. PyMuPDF writes the drawing operations of one page as SVG: the shapes match, but groups and document structure are gone. With text_as="paths" the text also stops being text. Treat PDF to SVG as "make this page drawable as SVG", not as a round trip.

docs.title: Rejected backends
docs.text: cairosvg as a default, pdf2image, svglib, reportlab, skia-python, pdfkit, weasyprint, and anything that needs Cairo, Poppler or Ghostscript at install time are excluded on purpose. A default backend must install as a self-contained wheel with no post-install step. CairoSVG and Ghostscript are reachable only through the opt-in extras. SPEC.md and IDEA.md in the repository record the full reasoning.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
The vexy-pdfsvgpy command is a Fire wrapper around the same functions the Python API uses. It is installed as a console script and can also run as python -m vexy_pdfsvgpy.

vexy-pdfsvgpy SUBCOMMAND [--flag VALUE ...]

Fire maps each keyword argument to a --flag. Boolean flags are switched on by naming them, for example --recursive. Run vexy-pdfsvgpy SUBCOMMAND --help to see the signature of one subcommand.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success. 1 The conversion failed. The CLI prints the error class and message, for example UnsupportedConversion: identity conversion png → png is not supported. 2 convert was called without --input or --output.

Fire also prints the integer return value (0, 1 or 2) on its own line.

docs.title: convert
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input IN --output OUT [flags]

Converts one file, or a directory of files, to another format. The input and output formats come from the file extensions (.pdf, .svg, .png, .jpg, .jpeg) unless you set them with a format spec.

docs.title: Format and backend flags
docs.text:
Flag Value Effect --input path Source file or directory. Required. --output path Destination file or directory. Required. --vinput format spec Input format, for example pdf_d. Overrides the extension. --voutput format spec Output format, for example svg_lt. Overrides the extension. --binput format spec Input format. Used only when --vinput is not given. --boutput format spec Output format. Used only when --voutput is not given. --hint hint codes Preferred backend, for example re or mu,ap. See Backends. --recursive switch With a directory input, search subdirectories too. --glob pattern With a directory input, select files with this glob pattern, for example "*/*.pdf". Files must still match the input format's extension. --text_as paths PDF to SVG or SVG normalization: convert text to outlines. Any other value, or no flag, keeps text as <text> elements. --verbose switch Set the log level to DEBUG. The CLI currently discards log messages, so this adds no output.

The v and b flags take the same format specs. The CLI checks --vinput before --binput and --voutput before --boutput. See Format grammar.

docs.title: Transform flags
docs.text:
convert also accepts these flags:

--regularize, --dim, --scale, --top, --bottom, --left, --right, --crop, --gray, --invert, --vivid, --bright, --contrast, --backdrop.

Transform flags are not wired up yet

In the current release these flags are passed unchanged to the backend function. No backend accepts them, so a conversion that uses one fails with exit code 1, for example:

BackendFailure:  pdf_to_png failed: pdf_to_png() got an unexpected keyword argument 'gray'

The exception is a same-format conversion such as PDF to PDF, where the CLI ignores extra options. The regularize subcommand relies on this. The size, crop and color operations exist as library modules (vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.sizecrop and vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.color) but are not yet called by convert.

docs.title: Directory input
docs.text:
When --input is a directory:

  1. Set the input format with --vinput or --binput. Without it, the call fails with Must specify explicit format specifier (e.g. --binput png_d) for directories.
  2. Use packaging d for the input format, for example pdf_d. Other packaging codes reject a directory.
  3. The command collects files with the matching extension (in both cases, for example *.pdf and *.PDF) from the directory, from its subdirectories with --recursive, or by --glob.
  4. With an output packaging of d, the command creates the output directory and writes one <stem>.<format> file per input.

The summary table shows the last file written.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Extension-driven
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report.png

# PDF to SVG with outlined text
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report.svg --text_as paths

# Prefer Apple Quartz for PDF to PNG (macOS only)
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report.png --hint ap

# Every PDF under ./pdfs, including subfolders, to ./pngs/<stem>.png
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input pdfs --output pngs --vinput pdf_d --boutput png_d --recursive

docs.title: regularize
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy regularize --input IN --output OUT [--hint CODES] [--verbose]

Runs convert with regularize=True. Use the same format on both sides:

  • PDF to PDF uses the pdf_normalize capability: pymupdf re-saves the document with clean=True, deflate=True and garbage=4. --hint ap uses Apple PDFKit on macOS instead.
  • SVG to SVG uses svg_normalize: pymupdf opens the SVG and writes the first page back out as SVG.
vexy-pdfsvgpy regularize --input messy.pdf --output clean.pdf

docs.title: split
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy split --input IN.pdf [--out_dir DIR] [--verbose]

Writes one PDF per page with pikepdf, without re-encoding the pages. Without --out_dir, the files go next to the input. File names follow {stem}-pikepdf-page-{NN}.pdf; the page number has at least two digits.

vexy-pdfsvgpy split --input book.pdf --out_dir ./pages/
# Split book.pdf into 3 page(s) in pages

docs.title: merge
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy merge --inputs "A.pdf,B.pdf,..." [--output OUT.pdf] [--verbose]

Concatenates PDFs with pikepdf, in the order given. --inputs is one comma-separated string. Without --output, the result is <first-stem>-merged.pdf next to the first input.

vexy-pdfsvgpy merge --inputs "a.pdf,b.pdf,c.pdf" --output book.pdf
# Merged 3 file(s) into book.pdf

docs.title: version
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy version

Prints the package version.

docs.title: Format shortcuts
docs.text:
Every valid format spec that contains an underscore is also a subcommand. The shortcut runs convert with --voutput set to that spec and accepts all other convert flags:

# Same as: vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input a.pdf --output a.svg --voutput svg_s
vexy-pdfsvgpy svg_s --input a.pdf --output a.svg

Bare names such as pdf or svg are not registered. The CLI registers these 35 shortcuts:

Format Shortcuts PDF pdf_d, pdf_db, pdf_do, pdf_dt, pdf_l, pdf_lb, pdf_lo, pdf_lt, pdf_m, pdf_mb, pdf_mo, pdf_mt, pdf_s, pdf_sb, pdf_so, pdf_st SVG svg_d, svg_db, svg_do, svg_dt, svg_l, svg_lb, svg_lo, svg_lt, svg_s, svg_sb, svg_so, svg_st PNG png_d, png_l, png_m, png_s JPG jpg_d, jpg_m, jpg_s

The top-level vexy-pdfsvgpy --help does not list subcommands, because Fire shows only the class description. Use vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --help to see the flags of convert.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Python 3.12 or later, uv and git.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdfsvgpy.git
cd vexy-pdfsvgpy

  2. Install the package and the dev dependency group (pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, mypy, lxml-stubs):

    uv sync --dev

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
These are the commands CI runs (.github/workflows/ci.yml):

uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ruff format --check src tests
uv run mypy src/vexy_pdfsvgpy
uv run pytest -q

mypy runs in strict mode. Backends without type information (vtracer, pypdfium2, ghostscript, cairosvg, resvg_py, fire, Foundation, Quartz) are listed in [[tool.mypy.overrides]] in pyproject.toml.

CI runs the tests on Ubuntu and macOS with Python 3.12 and 3.13.

./test.sh runs the maintainer's full post-edit chain: autoflake, pyupgrade, ruff check --fix, ruff format and uvx hatch test. It needs fd.

docs.title: Test fixtures
docs.text:
Tests read small committed files from tests/fixtures/: three synthetic PDFs (fontlab_posters.pdf, papercut.pdf, regularity.pdf) and SVGs (hello_glyphs.svg, initial.svg, tiger.svg). Regenerate the PDFs with:

uv run python tests/fixtures/_generate.py

The larger real-world samples in testdata/ are not in git and are not needed to run the tests. The scripts in examples/ read from testdata/.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
examples/ holds runnable scripts that use the public API:

Script What it does convert_coupon.py Splits a PDF, rasterizes each page at 300 dpi, merges the results trace_logo.py SVG → PNG → traced SVG round trip through vtracer layer_stack.py Stacks SVGs into a layered SVG and a layered PDF with OCGs regularize_batch.py Normalizes every fixture in testdata/

Run one with uv run examples/trace_logo.py.

docs.title: Add or change a backend
docs.text:
1. Read IDEA.md and SPEC.md §2 first. A default backend must install as a self-contained wheel with no system library.
  2. Add a module under src/vexy_pdfsvgpy/backends/. Functions take src: Path, dst: Path plus keyword-only options, return dst, and raise RuntimeError("[name] op failed: ...").
  3. Register the functions in dispatch._load_table() inside try/except ImportError, with a Hint.
  4. Add tests under tests/backends/.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation source is in src_docs/md/, and the site configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. ProperDocs with the MaterialX theme builds it into docs/, which GitHub Pages serves at https://vexy.dev/vexy-pdfsvgpy/.

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ on every push to main that changes src_docs/. Do not edit docs/ by hand.

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./build.sh package   # uv build + twine check into dist/
./build.sh docs      # documentation only
./build.sh           # both

The version comes from the git tag through hatch-vcs. The build writes it into src/vexy_pdfsvgpy/_version.py, which is not tracked.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
Releases are tagged vX.Y.Z. Two paths publish to PyPI:

  • ./publish.sh runs gitnextver, which commits pending changes, tags the next version and pushes. It then builds from the tag and uploads with uv publish. It needs a PyPI credential such as UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN.
  • The Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) runs on every pushed v* tag. It builds the sdist and wheel, checks them with twine, and uploads with PyPI trusted publishing. It skips files that are already on PyPI, so it does not fail after publish.sh has uploaded the same version.

Record changes in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Format grammar
docs.text: File extensions cover the common case: report.pdf is a PDF and report.png is a PNG. When you need to say more, such as "a folder of PDFs" or "a layered SVG", you pass a format spec through vinput/voutput or binput/boutput.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
A format spec is a format name, optionally followed by an underscore and one or two qualifier letters:

{format}[_{packaging}[{content}]]
  • format is pdf, svg, png or jpg.
  • packaging is one letter: d, m, l or s.
  • content is one letter: o, t or b. Only vector formats (pdf, svg) take it.

Letters are case-insensitive. A qualifier can be omitted when it equals the default.

Qualifier Code Meaning Packaging d (default) Collection of single files: one output per input. Packaging m Multi-page file. Packaging l Layered single-page file. Packaging s Single-page file. Content (vector only) o (default) Outlines: text as paths. Content (vector only) t Text with embedded fonts. Content (vector only) b Bitmap only.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
FormatSpec.parse() rejects these combinations with InvalidInput:

  • An unknown format, packaging or content letter.
  • A content letter on png or jpg: png_lo fails.
  • svg_m: SVG has no multi-page form.
  • jpg_l: JPG has no layered form.
  • More than two qualifier letters: pdf_mot fails.
  • An empty spec or an empty qualifier such as pdf_.

png_m and jpg_m are accepted by the parser.

docs.title: Defaults and canonical form
docs.text:
When the content letter is omitted on a vector format, it becomes o. str(spec) returns the shortest form that parses back to the same spec:

from vexy_pdfsvgpy import FormatSpec

FormatSpec.parse("pdf_do").__str__()   # 'pdf'
str(FormatSpec.parse("pdf_m"))         # 'pdf_mo'
str(FormatSpec.parse("png_l"))         # 'png_l'
str(FormatSpec.parse("svg_lt"))        # 'svg_lt'

FormatSpec.from_extension(path) maps .pdf, .svg, .png, .jpg and .jpeg to the default spec for that format. Any other extension raises InvalidInput.

docs.title: What the qualifiers change today
docs.text:
In the current release, convert() uses the spec like this:

  • Format chooses the conversion. The planner looks only at the input and output format names. See Architecture.
  • Input packaging d allows a directory input. convert() collects every file with the matching extension and converts each one. Any other input packaging rejects a directory with InvalidInput.
  • Output packaging d treats an output path that is an existing directory, or has no extension, as a directory. convert() creates it and writes <stem>.<format> inside.
  • Several inputs with output packaging m or l raise NotImplementedError. Combining many files into one multi-page or layered document is not wired into convert() yet. The reshape functions docs2pages_pdf, docs2layers_pdf and docs2layers_svg in vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.reshape do this directly; see Python API.
  • Content is parsed and stored but does not select a backend or option. To outline text in PDF to SVG, use text_as="paths".

docs.title: Example: a folder of PDFs
docs.text:
from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert

# Rasterize page 1 of every PDF in ./pdfs/ into ./pngs/<stem>.png
convert(input="./pdfs/", output="./pngs/", binput="pdf_d", boutput="png_d")

Step by step, for a folder containing a.pdf and b.pdf:

  1. binput="pdf_d" parses to format pdf, packaging d, content o.
  2. Because the input is a directory and the packaging is d, convert() collects a.pdf and b.pdf.
  3. boutput="png_d" parses to format png, packaging d.
  4. The planner picks the pdf_to_png capability for each file.
  5. convert() creates ./pngs/ and writes ./pngs/a.png and ./pngs/b.png.
  6. The call returns [Path('pngs/a.png'), Path('pngs/b.png')].

docs.title: Flag precedence
docs.text: vinput wins over binput, and voutput wins over boutput. Both pairs accept any format spec; the v/b prefix does not restrict the format.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later.
  • A platform with wheels for the dependencies. CI tests Ubuntu and macOS. The Apple Quartz backend (hint ap) works only on macOS.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
uvpipuv tool (CLI only) 
uv add vexy-pdfsvgpy

pip install vexy-pdfsvgpy

uv tool install vexy-pdfsvgpy

The install pulls these runtime dependencies:

Package Role pymupdf PDF to PNG, PDF to SVG, SVG to PDF, normalization pypdfium2 Alternate PDF to PNG renderer pypdf Pure-Python PDF split and merge pikepdf Lossless PDF split and merge resvg-py SVG to PNG through the Rust resvg renderer vtracer PNG or JPG to SVG tracing Pillow Bitmap metadata and color operations lxml Layered SVG composition and splitting fire, loguru, rich CLI, logging, terminal output pyobjc-framework-Quartz, pyobjc-framework-Cocoa macOS only: the ap backend

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Two backends sit behind extras because they need system libraries, which the core package avoids.

pip install "vexy-pdfsvgpy[cairo]"        # CairoSVG, used by hint "ca"
pip install "vexy-pdfsvgpy[ghostscript]"  # Ghostscript bindings, used by hint "gs"
pip install "vexy-pdfsvgpy[all]"          # both

The cairo extra needs the Cairo library on the system. The ghostscript extra needs a Ghostscript installation. Without them, the ca and gs hints fail when the conversion runs.

docs.title: Check the install
docs.text:
1. Print the version:

    vexy-pdfsvgpy version

    The command prints the installed version.

  2. Check the import from Python:

    python -c "import vexy_pdfsvgpy; print(vexy_pdfsvgpy.__version__)"

You can also run the package as a module: python -m vexy_pdfsvgpy version.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdfsvgpy.git
cd vexy-pdfsvgpy

  2. Create the environment with the development tools:

    uv sync --dev

  3. Run the CLI from the checkout:

    uv run vexy-pdfsvgpy version

The version comes from the latest git tag through hatch-vcs, so a checkout between releases reports a development version such as 0.0.6.dev2+g996b83d04.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page follows one PDF through the main operations. Each step shows the CLI command first and the Python call second.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• vexy-pdfsvgpy is installed. See Installation.
  • You have a PDF file. The examples use report.pdf.

docs.title: Rasterize a PDF page to PNG
docs.text:
1. Run the conversion:

    vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report.png

  2. Read the summary table. It lists the input path, the output path and the output size in bytes.

The default backend, pymupdf, renders the first page (page=0) at 300 dpi. The same call from Python:

from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert

out = convert(input="report.pdf", output="report.png")
print(out)  # report.png

convert() returns the output path as a pathlib.Path.

To render at another resolution, pass the backend keyword through convert():

convert(input="report.pdf", output="report-72dpi.png", dpi=72)

Extra keyword arguments go straight to the backend function. The pymupdf PDF renderer accepts page, dpi and alpha. See Python API.

docs.title: Convert a PDF page to SVG
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report.svg

By default the SVG keeps text as <text> elements. To turn every glyph into an outline, add --text_as paths:

vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input report.pdf --output report-outlined.svg --text_as paths

The outlined SVG renders the same without the fonts, but the text can no longer be selected or edited.

docs.title: Convert an SVG to PDF and PNG
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input logo.svg --output logo.pdf
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input logo.svg --output logo.png

SVG to PNG uses resvg-py by default and renders at 2048 pixels wide. To use pymupdf instead, which renders at 300 dpi, add --hint mu:

vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input logo.svg --output logo.png --hint mu

docs.title: Trace a bitmap to SVG
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input scan.png --output scan.svg

vtracer traces the bitmap into color spline paths. JPG input works the same way.

docs.title: Wrap a bitmap in a PDF
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input scan.png --output scan.pdf

The bitmap is placed in a one-page PDF without tracing.

docs.title: Split and merge PDFs
docs.text:
1. Split a multi-page PDF into one file per page:

    vexy-pdfsvgpy split --input book.pdf --out_dir ./pages/

    For a three-page book.pdf, the result is pages/book-pikepdf-page-01.pdf, pages/book-pikepdf-page-02.pdf and pages/book-pikepdf-page-03.pdf.

  2. Merge PDFs back into one file:

    vexy-pdfsvgpy merge --inputs "pages/book-pikepdf-page-01.pdf,pages/book-pikepdf-page-03.pdf" --output short.pdf

    The pages appear in the order of the comma-separated list.

docs.title: Normalize a PDF
docs.text:
vexy-pdfsvgpy regularize --input messy.pdf --output clean.pdf

pymupdf re-saves the file with cleaned content streams, deflate compression and unused objects removed (garbage=4).

docs.title: Convert a whole folder
docs.text:
A directory input needs an explicit format spec that says which files to pick up. The d packaging code means "a collection of single files":

from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert

paths = convert(input="./pdfs/", output="./pngs/", binput="pdf_d", boutput="png_d")

The call converts every *.pdf in ./pdfs/ (not recursively) and writes ./pngs/<stem>.png for each. It returns a list of output paths when more than one file matched. See Format grammar.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• CLI reference lists every flag.
  • Backends explains hints.
  • Troubleshooting lists current limitations.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists the errors you are most likely to see, what causes them, and what to do. Error messages are quoted as the CLI prints them.

docs.title: Known limitations in the current release
docs.text: Limitation Effect Workaround Transform flags are not wired up --gray, --invert, --vivid, --bright, --contrast, --backdrop, --dim, --scale, --top, --bottom, --left, --right, --crop and --regularize fail in cross-format conversions Convert first, then post-process with another tool. Use regularize only for PDF→PDF or SVG→SVG. Only the first page is converted PDF→PNG and PDF→SVG write page 1 Pass page=N from Python (zero-based), or split the PDF first and convert each page No multi-input composition in convert() Several inputs with output packaging m or l raise NotImplementedError Use merge, or vexy_pdfsvgpy.operations.reshape.docs2layers_pdf / docs2layers_svg No JPG output Any conversion to .jpg raises UnsupportedConversion Write PNG and convert it with Pillow Content qualifier has no effect pdf_mt behaves like pdf_mo Use text_as="paths" for outlines Output templates are not applied {page:02d} in --output is not expanded Name the output file yourself

docs.title: Error: --input and --output are required
docs.text: Exit code 2. Every convert call, and every format shortcut, needs both flags.

docs.title: InvalidInput: Cannot infer format from extension '.tif'; ...
docs.text: The format comes from the extension, and only .pdf, .svg, .png, .jpg and .jpeg are known. Rename the file or give an explicit spec with --vinput/--voutput.

docs.title: InvalidInput: Must specify explicit format specifier (e.g. --binput png_d) for directories
docs.text: A directory input has no extension. Add --vinput pdf_d (or svg_d, png_d, jpg_d) to say which files to collect.

docs.title: InvalidInput: No matching files found in ...
docs.text: The directory has no files with the extension of the input format. Check the format, or add --recursive if the files are in subfolders.

docs.title: InvalidInput: Unknown hint 'xx'; expected one of [...]
docs.text: Valid hint codes are ap, ca, gs, mu, pk and re.

docs.title: UnsupportedConversion: identity conversion png → png is not supported
docs.text: Same-format conversion exists only for PDF and SVG (normalization).

docs.title: UnsupportedConversion: no direct path pdf → jpg
docs.text: The planner supports only the pairs listed in Architecture.

docs.title: BackendFailure: [resvg] svg_to_png failed: svg_to_png() got an unexpected keyword argument 'dpi'
docs.text:
An option was passed to a backend that does not accept it. resvg takes width; pymupdf takes dpi. Either change the option or select the other backend with a hint:

vexy-pdfsvgpy convert --input logo.svg --output logo.png --hint mu

From Python, convert(..., hints="mu", dpi=96).

docs.title: BackendFailure: ... No module named 'ghostscript' or 'cairosvg'
docs.text:
The gs or ca hint was used without the extra. Install it:

pip install "vexy-pdfsvgpy[ghostscript]"   # or [cairo]

These extras also need the Ghostscript or Cairo system library.

docs.title: BackendFailure: [apple] ... unsupported on linux
docs.text: The ap hint works only on macOS. Remove it on other platforms. A fallback such as --hint ap,mu does not help: the dispatcher picks the backend before it runs, so ap,mu selects Apple on every platform.

docs.title: Text in the SVG uses the wrong font
docs.text: By default PDF→SVG keeps text as <text> elements that refer to fonts by name. A viewer without those fonts substitutes others. Use --text_as paths to draw glyphs as outlines.

docs.title: The PNG from an SVG has an unexpected size
docs.text: resvg renders at 2048 pixels wide by default, whatever the SVG's own size. Pass width= from Python, or use --hint mu to render at 300 dpi relative to the SVG's size.

docs.title: The PNG from a PDF is very large
docs.text: pymupdf renders at 300 dpi. From Python, pass a lower dpi, for example dpi=96.

docs.title: Get debug output
docs.text:
--verbose sets the log level to DEBUG, but in the current release the CLI sends log messages to a sink that discards them, so the flag adds no output. For a full Python traceback, call the API directly:

python -c "from vexy_pdfsvgpy import convert; convert(input='in.pdf', output='out.png')"

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text: Open an issue at https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdfsvgpy/issues with the command, the full error, the output of vexy-pdfsvgpy version, your Python version and your operating system.
